title: Agreement Between Subjective and Objective Refraction Using Autorefraction, Ray-Tracing, and Hartmann–Shack Aberrometry in Untreated Eyes Versus Eyes After Laser In Situ Keratomileusis
summary: This study aims to investigate how reliably different automated devices can measure refractive errors after laser vision correction surgery. In addition, untreated eyes will also be examined for comparison. During a single study visit, refractive error will first be determined by an optician. Afterwards, three additional contact-free measurements will be performed using different devices. The results of the different measurement methods will then be compared.

interventions.name: Measurement of patients without prior ocular treatment
Measurement of patients after laser in situ keratomileusis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients ≥ 18 years of age
- Patients with LASIK in at least one eye performed more than 6 months prior to study inclusion, or patients without prior corneal treatment and otherwise healthy eyes
- Sufficient physical and mental ability to cooperate during the examinations
Exclusion criteria:
-Patients with anterior or posterior segment abnormalities that may affect visual acuity or measurement accuracy (e.g. corneal scars, keratoconus, ectasia, advanced glaucoma, and/or macular degeneration)
- Visual acuity < 0.5
